reasons: The rules for captain and vice-captain scoring are not in this file.

terms.meaning: players chosen by a fan whose scores count for more, according to rules not shown here

sections.name: File setup, matchSelect
sections.title: Shared selections
sections.what: Brings in the database client and the public user shape, and defines which match fields are returned.
sections.why: Likely reason: returns only the match fields the screens need.

sections.name: teamSelect, findMatch, listOpenMatches, findTeam, listTeams, sumCompletedPoints, listUsers
sections.title: Reading matches, teams and users
sections.what: Loads one match, the list of upcoming or live matches, one user's team for a match, all teams for a set of users, the summed points for finished matches, and public user details. Results are ordered by date or points.
sections.why: Likely reason: each read is narrow so pages load only what they show.
sections.watch_out: Team reads include other members' picks, so crew scoping in the service is what keeps them private.

sections.name: listBuilderPlayers, listRulePlayers
sections.title: Reading players for a match
sections.what: Loads players from the two teams in a match, with whether each is playing and recent season stats. Also loads players by ID for rule checks.
sections.why: Likely reason: the team builder needs playing status and stats, while rule checks need only the basic fields.

sections.name: insertTeam
sections.title: Saving a team
sections.what: Saves a new fantasy team with its captain, vice-captain and chosen players in one write.
sections.why: Likely reason: the team and its players are created together, so a team is never saved half complete.
sections.watch_out: One team per fan per match is enforced by a database rule, which the service must handle when it fails.

summary: Reads and writes match, team, player and standing data for contests.
purpose: Database access for the contest feature.
why: Likely reason: narrow queries return only what each page needs.
how: 1. Load matches and teams. 2. Load players with their playing status and stats. 3. Add up points for finished matches. 4. Save a team with its captain, vice-captain and players in one write.
inputs: Match IDs, user IDs, and team choices.
outputs: Match, team, user and player records, sums, or a saved team.
risks: Team reads include other members' picks, so privacy depends on the service layer checking membership.
debug: If a team is missing, check the match and user IDs. If saving a second team fails, check the duplicate conflict handling.
